summary: Re-review after the rework round: all six suggestions landed cleanly and introduced no new problems. Maya's restatement ('three signs won't sink me anymore. but i will bring it up at every dinner...') still reads as a $$ max with a one-star overshoot. It no longer copies level_17's bill-theatrics device, and its Spindrift and Mooring Post payoffs match it. 'months' gives the trip no date. Brooke's healthy line is now one clear wish with no junk-food backstory, in new words, and Halyard's 'battered and fried' reaction matches its tempura-and-panko reviews. Brooke's satay-incident callback keeps the peanut clue implied, alongside Cyrus's binned dressing. Maya's Starboard fail now rests on Cyrus's earlier warning and matches the review's peanut-miso dressing on most of the vegetable page plus the crushed-peanut spinach. Ropewalk's new quote keeps clear peanut-free evidence without the triple-'not' shape. Spindrift's 'a whole page of the menu' now matches Cyrus's and Mina's standard exactly, so the answer no longer looks weaker than Starboard on the vegetarian need, and Mooring Post no longer repeats Spindrift's crunch phrasing. On the writer's question: the craving clues in the opening 20% and the healthy line in the last 15% are not a fairness problem. The mid-conversation placement rule (narrative-writer brief v7, Validator check 12) applies only to buried levels, and this spec is implied. Both clues are clear and easy to find where they sit. On difficulty: the peanut clue is now properly implied and the craving never names sushi, but quiet, healthy, vegetarian and budget remain close to stated. So the level plays about as hard as levels 16-17, not a step up. The real challenge is telling five similar sushi counters apart from their reviews, which is fair. If Gabriella wants a steeper ramp, it should come from level_19's buried placement rather than more rework here.
